comparator.name: Liberal Arts and Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: Tilburg University's official 2026-2027 curriculum, checked 2026-09-29, publishes a complete 180-ECTS structure: a 36-ECTS interdisciplinary first-year core plus 24 ECTS in one of three majors; a second year with 12 ECTS of shared courses, 30 ECTS in the selected major and 18 ECTS in one societal theme; and a third year with a 30-ECTS mobility/minor window, Senior Seminar, Societal Capstone and Bachelor Thesis. Because the programme deliberately retains student choice among three majors and three themes and names no default route, these official structured choices are preserved as curriculum components rather than arbitrarily selecting one route. Zero-credit GROW activities are excluded. The credited components total exactly 180 ECTS.
components: European History: Politics, Religion, and Culture
Imagining Justice: An Introduction to Law, Politics, and Culture
Our Brain: An Introduction to Cognitive Neuroscience and Behavior
Individuals and Collectives: An Introduction to Interdisciplinary Social Sciences
A 24-ECTS structured choice among the official Interdisciplinary Social Sciences, Cognitive Neuroscience and Behavior, or Law, Politics, and Culture major curricula.
Thirty ECTS of compulsory and elective coursework within the selected major.
Eighteen ECTS selected within Transformations to Sustainability, Democracy and Justice, or Technology and Society.
One official 30-ECTS option: exchange, Humanities and Digital Sciences electives, or an approved minor.
A real-world project linked to the selected societal theme, often with an external partner.
Independent research within the selected major.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Interdisciplinary analysis of complex social issues across philosophy, law, sociology, psychology, neuroscience, politics and economics
Social structures, inequality, migration, diversity, polarisation and relationships between individuals and communities
Law, politics, culture, democracy, justice, power and institutions
Brain, behaviour, emotion, cognition, resilience and well-being
Interdisciplinary qualitative and quantitative research applied to real-world social challenges
adjacent: Transformations to sustainability and environmental governance
Technology and society, including algorithmic thinking, AI ethics and digital culture
questions: Structured major and societal-theme choices that let students combine depth with interdisciplinary breadth
Career and further-study trajectories in policy, research, public service, neuroscience, sustainability and consultancy

alternatives.label: Interdisciplinary society, behaviour & public challenges
alternatives.concept: A broad Liberal Arts and Sciences programme integrating sociology, politics, law, psychology, philosophy, research, sustainability and technology to examine complex societal challenges.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum balances social science, behavioural study, law and politics with sustainability, technology and interdisciplinary research, so the label foregrounds its integrated public-challenges focus.
progression: Introductory sociology, politics, brain and behaviour, research methods, law, sustainability and programming precede advanced public policy, psychology, sociology, philosophy and European law. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Cognitive neuroscience, behaviour & society
alternatives.concept: A Liberal Arts and Sciences direction centred on cognition, neuroscience, psychology and behavioural research, framed by sociology, politics, philosophy, data and social questions.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has a sequenced brain-and-behaviour, psychology, cognitive-neuroscience and research core while retaining social-science and philosophical breadth.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces most law, public-policy and sustainability coursework with a sustained cognitive-neuroscience and psychology sequence including neurobiology, perception, higher-order functions, psycholinguistics and advanced behavioural research.
progression: Brain-and-behaviour, sociology, philosophy, research methods and introductory psychology precede neurobiology, advanced psychology, perception, higher-order functions, psycholinguistics and research seminars. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Law, politics & contested culture
alternatives.concept: A Liberal Arts and Sciences direction focused on law, democracy, political institutions, philosophy, history, rhetoric, media and cultural meaning.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines a substantial law and politics sequence with philosophy, history, rhetoric, literature and media, so the label captures both institutional and cultural interpretation.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the other alternatives, this route replaces most psychology, neuroscience and sustainability coursework with public, international, constitutional, criminal, private and EU law plus political theory, history and cultural analysis.
progression: Foundations in law, society, philosophy and history precede international and constitutional law, political theory, research seminars, criminal and private law, EU law and advanced political and philosophical study. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match accounts for the shared interdisciplinary core, Interdisciplinary Social Sciences direction and all three societal themes. Cognitive Neuroscience and Behavior and Law, Politics, and Culture remain separate generator-backed directions with coherent feasible UCR curricula. The three completed curricula differ pairwise by well over four courses (30 ECTS), so production reaches the maximum of three alternatives.

notes.text: Tilburg combines a common Liberal Arts and Sciences core with an official major, societal theme and mobility choice. UCR can recreate three coherent interdisciplinary directions, but no single alternative reproduces every prescribed Tilburg major course, theme cluster, capstone partnership or the exact 12-ECTS Bachelor Thesis.
